In hospital environments, usage of AI tools is still somewhat restricted by health department restrictions as well as the general concern around AI usage in clinical work. This means that by extension, while there are people using some AI tools in limited approved contexts, or "down-low" in unapproved contexts, in general there is not free AI usage in hospital settings. This affects research which is conducted in hospital environments or be hospital personnel (even those who have a joint affiliation with a university). 

I would also say that knowledge of statistics in general is limited amongst clinical staff, and when clinical staff embark on research it is a hurdle for them to acquire these skills. At my health service we have a biostatician hired on a joint university/hospital affiliated role in order to consult on these matters. 

This is not to completely discourage AI usage altogether - although most librarians such as myself as skeptical and cautious about the technology - but just to reflect the fact that research conducted on a hospital level is going to be somewhat separated from other institutions because of this. It is something to keep in mind.
